prompt: A right triangle has sides of length $3$, $4$, and $5$. The HYPOTENUSE is the side across from the right angle, and it is always the longest. How long is the hypotenuse?
hint: The hypotenuse is always the longest side of a right triangle, across from the right angle.

hints.text: The hypotenuse is always the longest side of a right triangle, across from the right angle.
Compare the three side lengths $3$, $4$, and $5$, and pick the biggest one.
The longest side is $5$, so the hypotenuse is $5$.

explanation: The hypotenuse sits directly across from the $90^\circ$ corner of the triangle.
Because it faces the largest angle, it is always the longest of the three sides.
Of the lengths $3$, $4$, and $5$, the longest is $5$, so the hypotenuse is $5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check with Pythagoras
steps: If $5$ is the hypotenuse, then the squares of the two shorter sides must add up to its square.
Test it with the numbers: $3^2 + 4^2 = 9 + 16 = 25$, and $5^2 = 25$ as well.
The equation balances only with $5$ as the side across from the right angle, so the hypotenuse is $5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Draw it and look
steps: Sketch a right angle with one leg of $3$ going across and one leg of $4$ going up.
The slanted side joining the two free ends is the hypotenuse, since it faces the right angle.
That slant has to reach farther than either leg alone, so it must be the side of length $5$.
